approachQuestion.prompt:
Compare Release Labels

Two release labels consist of nonempty decimal components separated by dots. Compare components from left to right as nonnegative integers; leading zeroes do not matter. Missing trailing components mean zero. Return −1, 0, or 1 according to whether first is numerically less than, equal to, or greater than second under this rule. Components may be too long for built-in integers.

Example 1: first="3.00012.0", second="3.12" → 0.
Example 2: first="2.9", second="2.10" → −1.
Example 3: first="0.0.1", second="0" → 1.
Example 4: first="000", second="0.00" → 0.

Constraints:
1 ≤ each label length ≤ 200,000. Each label matches digits followed by zero or more dot-and-digits groups.
Each component has at least one digit; only digits 0–9 and dots occur.
Do not modify inputs or use arbitrary-precision integer libraries. Return one of −1,0,1.

options.text: Scan corresponding component boundaries in the originals. Skip leading zeroes within each component. Compare significant digit counts, then significant digits lexicographically if lengths tie. Treat a missing component as zero; return at the first difference, or 0 after both labels end.
options.feedback: Nonnegative decimal integers with different significant lengths compare by length; equal lengths compare by digit order. Leading zeroes and absent zero components are handled explicitly.

options.text: Split both labels into separate copied component strings, then compare their zero-trimmed significant digits by length and digit order, treating missing components as zero.
options.feedback: This follows the full rule and avoids numeric overflow, but copied component strings are removable when boundaries can be scanned in the original labels.

options.text: Compare the entire original label strings lexicographically, including dots and leading zeroes.
options.feedback: Text order differs from component numeric order. "2.9" compares lexicographically above "2.10", but component 9 is less than 10.

options.text: Convert each component to a signed 64-bit integer, then compare corresponding integers and use zero for missing components.
options.feedback: A legal component may have thousands of significant digits and cannot fit in 64 bits. The method cannot implement the full allowed domain.

feedback.reason: After ignoring leading zeros, a longer digit component represents a larger nonnegative integer; equal significant lengths permit lexicographic digit comparison.
details: Locate corresponding components in the original labels. Ignore their leading zeroes. Compare significant lengths and then equal-length digit ranges, treating an absent component as zero. Stop at the first difference or after both labels end.

After ignoring leading zeros, a longer digit component represents a larger nonnegative integer; equal significant lengths permit lexicographic digit comparison. This avoids overflow on arbitrarily long components. Missing components represent zero, so a trailing zero component alone cannot change equality.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Compare Significant Component Ranges”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let N be the sum of both label lengths. Reads of lengths and indexed characters, index arithmetic and digit comparisons cost constant time. No component strings are copied and no integer conversion or arbitrary-precision arithmetic is used. Include all boundary and digit scans. Exclude input and scalar output; include helper indices and stack. No hashing or recursion.
constraints: 1 ≤ each label length ≤ 200,000. Each label matches digits followed by zero or more dot-and-digits groups.
Each component has at least one digit; only digits 0–9 and dots occur.
Do not modify inputs or use arbitrary-precision integer libraries. Return one of −1,0,1.

options.text: O(log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Scan component ranges a bounded number of times without numeric conversion or copies.
details: Each component’s characters are visited a fixed number of times to find its end, skip zeroes and compare significant digits. Components never need to be converted or copied. Only a fixed set of boundaries and cursors are retained.
The option “O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Repeated visits within one component have bounded multiplicity, so total work is linear.
The option “O(N) time, O(N) auxiliary space.”: Copied component strings describe the partial alternative, not the fixed method.
The option “O(N²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The method does not compare each component with all other components.
The option “O(log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Equality can require reading both full labels.
